title: What If You Aimed a Laser at the Moon? Almost Nothing Returns

scenes.text: What if you aimed a laser at the Moon? Apollo astronauts left mirrors waiting there.
The light takes about 2.5 seconds to make the round trip, Earth to Moon and back.
By the time it arrives, the beam has spread to roughly 6.5 kilometers wide.
That's why almost nothing returns. Of 300 quadrillion photons sent, only about one to five make it home.
Scientists fire these pulses anyway. Counting that handful of photons measures the Moon's distance.
So yes, you can hit the Moon with a laser. You'd just never see the light come back.
